title: The Wedding Photo
script: Our wedding photo erased me. My wife was still there. I was gone. She stared at me. 'Who are you?' I showed her my ring. She reached for the phone. I grabbed the photo by its torn edge. My face came back. She put the phone down. 'What's wrong?' Then my face began to fade again. I held the frame tight, too scared to blink. My wife screamed. My hands were gone. I could not feel the frame. I tried to call her name. No sound came out. She reached towards me. Her fingers hit glass. Now I was inside the photo. Outside, a man held my wife. The man I had cut from our wedding photo just last night.

title: The Spare Key
script: Why did my key still fit? A stranger opened my door. My wife stood behind him. 'Please,' she said. 'Don't make me watch this again.' I pushed past them. My coat hung in its usual place. Two cups sat on the table. One was still warm. Then I saw my shoes by the stairs. They were wet. So were mine. The stranger locked the door. I reached for my wife, but she stepped back. Under the table lay a pile of keys like mine. The stranger took my hand. It felt like holding my own. 'How many times?' I asked. My wife began to cry. He turned my hand over. A small switch blinked beneath my skin. 'This one remembers coming home.'

title: The Last Bus
script: The bus driver had my face. He shut the doors before I could leave. 'Sit down,' he said. 'She's almost here.' I ran to the back. Every seat held my coat. Each coat was warm. At the next stop, a woman raised her hand. It was my wife. I shouted her name. She walked straight past my window. The driver shook his head. 'She can't see you yet.' I pulled the cord. All the coats turned towards me. There were men inside them now. All had my face. My wife stepped on and held up our wedding photo. The driver pointed at me. 'Try this one,' he said. 'He still thinks you're alive.'

title: The Wrong Voice
script: My door asked me to scream. The voice came from the new doorbell. 'Your wife is hurt. Scream if you want help.' I called her phone. It rang in the hall outside. Then her voice came through the door. 'Please let me in.' I reached for the lock. My phone lit up. A text from her said she was still at work. The voice outside began to cry. Then it stopped, right in the middle of a breath. Something scraped the lock. I held a chair against the door. My phone rang again. I heard my own scream. Then my own voice said, 'I've got it now.' From the hall, my wife asked why I was calling her.

title: The Empty Chair
script: Our empty chair began to breathe. My wife dropped her fork. 'Don't look at it,' she said. I kept my eyes on her. The chair slid closer. A wet hand closed round my wrist. I tried to stand, but it pulled me down. My wife set a third plate on the table. The hand let go. Then she put my food on that plate. A bite vanished. The chair scraped closer to her. I grabbed her arm. 'We have to leave.' She looked at my hand as if she had never seen it. 'No,' she whispered. 'It's finally working.' In the window, I saw the chair was full. I was the one with no face.
